executive_summary: AUD/USD trades at 0.70555 (5 August close), up 1.16% over one month, down 1.72% over three, up 2.59% over six and up 7.89% over twelve — a pair that has gone nowhere for a quarter while both legs of it have been repriced violently. The dominant bilateral fact is that both dossiers are bullish their own currency: the AUD dossier is tactically Bullish at conviction 3 on the highest policy rate in the G10+SGD, and the USD dossier is tactically Bullish at conviction 2 on a 147bp trade-weighted carry advantage and a Warsh Fed with three sitting hike dissenters. Those views do not cancel evenly — they cancel in a specific and tradeable way, because the one channel where they touch directly is the AU–US front-end spread, and that spread has compressed from +56bp to +35bp to +29bp on the 2Y and to just +18bp on the 10Y against the Treasury's own 31 July curve, while spot has risen. AUD/USD is approaching its prior swing high while the Australia-US 2-year yield spread continues to point lower, a divergence suggesting upside may be limited, and the pair has increasingly traded as a relative rates play rather than a pure risk proxy. The second bilateral insight neither standalone dossier can generate is that the Strait of Hormuz shock is no longer an AUD/USD-positive event: because the United States is now a net energy exporter earning a $63.61 Gulf Coast crack spread while Australia earns a JKM and coal windfall, the terms-of-trade transfer is positive-sum for both currencies and largely self-cancelling in this pair, which is precisely why a 78% year-on-year JKM rally has produced a flat three-month chart. Valuation corroborates from both sides independently: the AUD dossier's REER-derived fair value for AUD/USD is 0.6545 and the USD dossier's is 0.6513, so spot sits roughly 7.4–8.3% rich to real-effective fair value with the AUD REER at the 97th percentile and the USD REER at roughly the 52nd. We are tactically Bullish at conviction 2 (weighted score +0.1003) on a squeeze-prone positioning setup, a supportive risk regime, a live 11 August RBA Statement on Monetary Policy and a US fiscal term premium that has already proved dollar-negative; and strategically Bearish at conviction 3 (weighted score −0.2196) on rate-differential compression, real-effective overvaluation and a dollar smile shifting toward the US-exceptionalism leg. The caveat that caps tactical conviction is that the pair sits within 0.2 pips of its 100-day moving average beneath a dense 0.7079–0.7100 resistance shelf, with a carry-to-vol ratio of only 0.10 offering no cushion for being wrong.

market_context.valuation_assessment: The two dossiers arrive at the same bilateral conclusion from independent REER-relative derivations. The AUD dossier computes AUD 7.48% rich to USD with an implied fair value of AUD/USD 0.6545; the USD dossier computes USD 7.41% cheap to AUD with an implied fair value of 0.6513. Spot at 0.70555 therefore sits 7.4–8.3% above real-effective fair value on either method. Australia's BIS real broad effective exchange rate printed 115.92 in June 2026, +9.8% year-on-year and at the 97th percentile, while the US REER printed 107.84, -0.19% year-on-year, at roughly the 52nd percentile. AUD has already been paid for its carry, its terms of trade and its rate crown in real trade-weighted space, and USD has not been penalised for anything. What is priced at 0.70555 is a permanent 4.35% RBA cash rate, a permanent energy terms-of-trade windfall accruing to Australia and no consequence from Australia's A$27.1bn quarterly current account deficit — three assumptions of which the third is already demonstrably false.

market_context.recent_regime: The pair's regime since May has been a rangebound rates-versus-risk standoff in which the two currencies have been strong for the same reason — an energy-led global inflation shock that has both central banks talking hawkishly — and have therefore cancelled. AUD/USD's correlation with the Chinese yuan has weakened markedly, with the six-month correlation falling to 0.70 and the three-month correlation to 0.28. The last four weeks have been a recovery off the 0.6923 low of 29 July, driven by the dollar's loss of the 100 handle on 30 July rather than by anything Australian — the 29 July Australian CPI undershoot cut 11 August RBA hike odds from above 90% to roughly a coin flip, which should have hurt AUD and did not, indicating the dollar leg is the marginal driver.

bilateral_carry_analysis.breakeven_move: 72.5bp earns 6.04bp per month, which on spot 0.70555 is 4.3 pips. A one-month long position is erased if spot falls from 0.70555 to 0.70512. Over six months the cushion is 25 pips (to 0.70305).
bilateral_carry_analysis.carry_assessment: The carry on this pair is the worst available on any AUD cross and one of the worst in the G10 relative to its volatility, and that fact governs how the entire directional view must be expressed. Australia has out-yielded the United States since February 2026, but the carry-to-vol ratio is only 0.10 against 0.79 for AUD/CHF and 0.65 for AUD/SGD — AUD/USD delivers roughly one-eighth the risk-adjusted carry of the best available AUD expression. Carry is working in the sense that realised volatility is low and the risk backdrop has not produced negative-carry conditions, but it is not working in this pair, because 72.5bp of differential is too small to matter against a 7%+ vol. The pair is a directional trade dressed as a carry trade. The forward curve prices AUD to depreciate by less than half a percent annualised, far less than the 72.5bp policy differential implies, because the money-market differential is much narrower than the policy-rate differential — both directions are unusually cheap to express in forwards, a strong argument against paying option premium for a directional view.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The level of the differential favours AUD and the trajectory does not, and over four weeks the trajectory is what the pair is trading. Australia's 4.35% cash rate stands 72.5bp above the Fed funds midpoint of 3.625%, but the market-relevant expression of that gap — the front-end sovereign spread — has compressed from +56bp six weeks ago to +35bp and now to +29bp using the ACGB 2Y at 4.57% against the Treasury's own 31 July 2Y par yield of 4.28%. At the ten-year point the compression is more severe: ACGB 4.93% against UST 4.75% is only +18bp. Both front ends price hikes, which is the source of two-way risk — the US front end prices roughly 60% more tightening over twelve months than the Australian one does, the bilateral inversion of the headline carry story. Spot has risen 1.16% over a month during which the 2Y spread compressed roughly 6bp, so the pair is trading rich to its own dominant driver.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the arithmetic runs one way even if neither central bank does anything dramatic. Futures drift toward a Fed funds rate of roughly 4.00% by year-end on three July dissents for a hike and a June SEP median of 3.8% for end-2026, which would compress the policy differential from +72.5bp to about +35bp. CBA, NAB and ANZ all now expect no further RBA move in 2026 after the 29 July CPI undershoot, and CBA expects two cuts in 2027. Australia's yield advantage over the United States is the thinnest of its advantages: +210bp over the ECB and BoC, +335bp over the BoJ, +435bp over the SNB, but only +72.5bp over the Fed, so AUD/USD is uniquely exposed to the one peer converging upward fastest. Yield spreads have anticipated AUD/USD turns this cycle with a lead. The Fed's own 2027-2028 medians embed cuts that would reassert an Australian premium, but that sits beyond the six-month window.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The differentials are small and the surprises have been symmetric. Australia grew 2.5% y/y against the US at 2.1% (+40bp), but the latest quarter inverts it. Headline inflation is 3.8% in Australia against 3.5% in the US (+30bp) and core is 3.6% trimmed mean against 3.3% core PCE (+30bp). The like-for-like trimmed-mean comparison — RBA 3.6% against Dallas Fed trimmed mean PCE 2.2% — is a +140bp gap, arguing for a stickier RBA and bullish AUD/USD. Against it, the direction of the next surprise favours the dollar: Australia's headline decline was driven by fuel excluded from the trimmed mean, while the US June headline fell on an energy drop that is now reversing, so the 12 August US CPI mechanically re-accelerates while Australia's next quarterly print is not until 28 October. Labour markets favour Australia clearly, but the US calendar dominates the tactical window.

The counterweight is Australia's demand side — real wages fell 0.8%, consumer sentiment and business confidence sit in bottom deciles — a cost-push, income-squeeze configuration rather than a wage-price spiral, arguing inflation fades without further tightening.

AUD/USD's beta to that rotation is high, and rising relative to the China channel — the six-month AUD/USD-CNY correlation has fallen to 0.70 and three-month to 0.28. The transmission is via the dollar smile — the pair sits at the bottom of the smile, the single position that favours AUD/USD.

AUD has the most negative convexity to a risk-regime shift of any G10 currency — the reference case is a fall from 0.80 to 0.55 in weeks during 2020 — while USD sits on the other side with a haven bid. AUD/USD's distribution is asymmetric by construction: the upside from regime continuation is bounded by a 97th-percentile real exchange rate and a 72.5bp carry, while the downside from regime change is measured in figures rather than pips. The regime is priced for continuation despite an active naval blockade, China's manufacturing PMI back in contraction at 49.2, Q2 GDP at 4.3% (weakest since Q4 2022) and a PBoC that has delivered zero cuts in 2026. Two pro-cyclical AUD flow channels compound this — superannuation equity-hedge rebalancing and Japanese retail carry demand — and both reverse in the same scenario with no USD-side offset.

strategic.score_interpretation: A net score of -0.2196 is a moderately bearish reading for the pair and is materially stronger in absolute terms than the tactical +0.1003. Its construction is more coherent: five factors are Bearish (-0.3294 gross), two are Bullish (+0.1098 gross) and three are Neutral. The dominant contributor is Policy & Rates at -0.1392, 42% of the gross negative, followed by Terms of Trade at -0.0624 and USD Funding at -0.0600. The two bearish channels beyond rates — risk-appetite convexity and the dollar smile — are the same underlying scenario expressed twice, so the score is less diversified than the factor count suggests. Against them stands the highest-confidence single reading in the analysis, Fiscal & Sovereign Risk at Bullish 62.
strategic.rationale: At strategic weights the four heaviest factors are Policy & Rates at 0.24, Guidance and USD Funding at 0.12 each and Terms of Trade at 0.12 — 0.60 of the total — and three of those four are Bearish or Neutral for the pair, which is the arithmetic behind a -0.2196 score. The dominant claim is rate-differential compression on every axis simultaneously: futures drift toward a Fed funds rate near 4.00% on three July hike dissents and a June SEP median of 3.8%, which would take the policy differential from +72.5bp to about +35bp, while CBA, NAB and ANZ all expect no further RBA move in 2026 and CBA expects two cuts in 2027. The AU-US 10Y spread at +18bp is already so thin that a single 25bp relative move inverts it. The dossiers reinforce rather than conflict at this horizon: the AUD dossier is strategically Neutral on rate convergence and a 97th-percentile real exchange rate, and the USD dossier is strategically Bullish on a durable trade-weighted carry advantage and the energy terms-of-trade flip, and the bilateral netting is unambiguously bearish AUD/USD. The bilateral-specific factors run in the same direction: the energy terms-of-trade shock is close to self-cancelling because the United States is a net energy exporter; the Hormuz payoff is concave for the pair, with escalation pair-negative and resolution only weakly positive; and the pair sits at the bottom of the dollar smile with negative convexity in both directions, and both available transitions — US exceptionalism at 4.00% funds, or crisis risk-off — are pair-negative. The forward at 0.70386 embeds only a -0.48% annualised discount, while UBS forecasts 0.73 in September and 0.74 in December and OCBC 0.73 end-2026, all of which require Australia to retain both its rate advantage and its 97th-percentile real exchange rate. We expect 0.6900 at six months, roughly 250 pips below the survey consensus and 400 below UBS's December target, because two independent REER derivations put fair value at 0.6513-0.6545 and neither has been marked. The path of least resistance is a slow erosion punctuated by carry-supported rallies rather than a break, because 72.5bp of carry is small but not zero. The dated catalysts that decide it are 16 September, 30 September, 28 October, 3 November, 10 November, and 8-9 December. The conviction driver that keeps this from being higher than 3 is the single opposing factor: at Bullish 62, US fiscal and sovereign risk is the highest-confidence reading in the analysis, and July demonstrated that a term-premium sell-off in Treasuries can push the dollar lower despite widening carry — if that channel dominates for two more quarters, the pair rises even as the rate differential compresses, and that is precisely the mechanism by which this thesis fails.
strategic.g10_relative_ranking: Short AUD/USD ranks 3rd of 8 as a strategic expression of AUD caution, behind short AUD/NZD (the purest fundamental divergence in the complex) and short AUD/NOK (only +10bp of carry to fight, a Norges Bank path that would invert it, and a 15.59%-of-GDP Norwegian current account surplus against Australia's 3.68% deficit). AUD/USD ranks ahead of short AUD/CAD, AUD/CHF, AUD/SGD and AUD/JPY, all of which require fighting 210-435bp of carry. As a strategic long-dollar expression the pair ranks 5th of 10, behind long USD/CHF, long USD/JPY, long USD/CAD and long USD/SEK. The reason AUD/USD ranks mid-table on both sides of the ledger is the same: a -72.5bp carry against the position means a short pays away 4.3 pips a month, so the trade needs the spot move to arrive, and this pair's spot moves are noisier than any comparable expression.

consensus_divergence.why_we_differ: Three specific analytical differences. First, aggregation: consensus reads Australia's rate crown as durable, but the crown is held against an equally weighted G10 while AUD/USD is exposed only to the peer converging fastest — the Fed is priced toward 4.00% with three sitting hike dissenters, and the AU-US 10Y spread at +18bp is already so thin that a single relative move inverts it. Second, the terms-of-trade sign flip: consensus trades oil through the pre-shale correlation in which higher crude is dollar-negative and AUD-positive, when the United States is now a net energy exporter earning a $63.61 Gulf Coast crack spread, which converts a 78% JKM rally from a pair-bullish event into a roughly neutral one and converts a Hormuz escalation from pair-bullish into pair-bearish. Third, valuation: both dossiers independently derive an AUD/USD real-effective fair value of 0.6513-0.6545, with Australia's REER at the 97th percentile and +9.8% year-on-year against a US REER at roughly the 52nd percentile and -0.19%, so consensus is implicitly forecasting that a 97th-percentile real exchange rate persists and extends. Consensus is also underweighting the deterioration in Australia's balance of payments while overweighting the terms-of-trade price gain that produced it.

cross_horizon_consistency.explanation: The mechanical driver is that four factors change sign or magnitude between horizons while Factor 1 stays bearish and deepens. Risk Appetite moves from Bullish 58 to Bearish 54 as its weight falls and the distribution's negative convexity dominates. Flows & Positioning moves from Bullish to Bearish as the population setting price changes from marginal speculators to reserve managers and portfolio allocators. Terms of Trade moves from Neutral to Bearish as its weight triples and the observable shifts from commodity prices (which cancel bilaterally) to external flows (which favour the dollar). USD Funding moves from Neutral to Bearish as abundant quantity resolves and the price of dollars keeps rising. Only Inflation & Growth and Fiscal & Sovereign Risk strengthen on the pair's bullish side. Underlying it all: over 2-4 weeks the level of Australia's rate advantage is what pays; over 1-6 months the change in that advantage is what prices, and the change is one-way.
cross_horizon_consistency.inflection_point: Mid-September 2026, specifically the 16 September FOMC and Summary of Economic Projections, the first meeting since forward guidance was deleted at which the Committee must publish a dot distribution. A secondary and earlier inflection is 12 August, when the US CPI energy base effect either delivers the hawkish re-acceleration expected or fails to.
cross_horizon_consistency.trading_implication: Run the tactical long through the 11-12 August RBA/US CPI cluster, then flatten rather than carrying an outright long into September. Express the tactical view in the one-month forward with a stop below 0.6950; take profit into the 0.7079-0.7100 shelf. Convert to strategic shorts from mid-September, preferring AUD/NZD and AUD/NOK to AUD/USD because those expressions do not require paying away 72.5bp of carry. Own six-month AUD/USD downside convexity struck below 0.6900 through the September-November window rather than holding spot shorts through the US domestic-negative cluster.

catalysts.event: RBA Monetary Policy Board decision + August Statement on Monetary Policy
catalysts.rationale: The dominant Australian event of the window. Even on the modal hold, the SoMP must mark export-price assumptions to a spot complex running 91-114% above Treasury Budget parameters and must abandon the May baseline's assumption that the conflict is resolved soon. Retention of the tightening clause is roughly half priced; a 25bp hike would widen the policy differential to +97.5bp and squeeze the ~40,000-contract legacy AUD short.

June's US headline fell 0.4% month-on-month, the largest decline since April 2020, entirely because energy dropped 5.7% during the brief post-ceasefire oil collapse. Brent has since traded between $86.99 and $105.32, so the energy component mechanically reverses. We expect headline to re-accelerate toward 3.7-4.0% with core near 2.6%, keeping the September FOMC live and compressing the AU-US differential — bearish for the pair, with no offsetting Australian re-acceleration since Australia's own fuel decline is excluded from the RBA's trimmed mean.

Norges Bank holds at 4.25%, just 10bp below the RBA, with a published forecast just above 4.5% at end-2026. A hike would strip Australia of the highest policy rate in the G10+SGD for the first time this cycle, removing the single strongest talking point in the AUD bull case and re-rating the carry-ranking narrative that supports AUD/USD longs. USD/NOK's 4.37% July fall shows where the relative-value flow goes instead.

catalysts.event: Expiry of the 60-day no-charge Strait of Hormuz transit window (Article 5 of the 17 June US-Iran memorandum)
catalysts.rationale: The memorandum granted safe passage with no charge for 60 days only from 17 June, so the window lapses around 16 August, and Iran has signalled transit fees. Escalation lifts Australia's terms of trade but delivers the United States a haven bid and a terms-of-trade gain as a net energy exporter, while hitting AUD through the highest risk beta in the G10 — so escalation is pair-negative, contrary to the market's framing. There is no visible volatility kink at this tenor.

catalysts.event: Minutes of the 28-29 July FOMC meeting
catalysts.rationale: The minutes will reveal how close the Committee came to hiking, given three dissents for a 25bp increase against a unanimous hold six weeks earlier and a June record showing many other participants saw the appropriate end-2026 rate above the current range. A hawkish internal distribution compresses the AU-US differential and pressures the pair.

June showed unemployment steady at 4.4% with employment up 76,300, the single strongest pillar of the RBA's capacity-pressure diagnosis. A rise in unemployment above 4.6% would materially weaken the case for any further RBA tightening and, combined with a compressing 2Y spread, would open 0.6950. A repeat of June's strength would restore hike optionality into the 29 September meeting.

catalysts.event: Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium (through 29 August)
catalysts.rationale: Chair Warsh's first Jackson Hole. He has used every prior venue to reinforce the 2% commitment and has openly asked how much accommodation the balance sheet is providing, which makes balance-sheet policy a live topic in a year when reserves have fallen $355.2bn. Any signal that a September increase is on the table validates the three dissenters, compresses the differential and pressures the pair.

catalysts.event: RBNZ Monetary Policy Statement + Bank of Canada decision + ABS Q2 National Accounts
catalysts.rationale: The heaviest single day in the strategic calendar for AUD relative value. The RBNZ, having hiked to 2.50% and stated further increases appear likely, is expected to hike again toward 3.00-3.25%, compressing the AU-NZ spread and draining relative-value demand from AUD longs into NZD. Australian Q2 GDP follows the March quarter's weak 0.3% print. For AUD/USD the transmission is indirect but consistent — Australia's carry story is eroding against every peer simultaneously.

catalysts.event: FOMC decision + Summary of Economic Projections
catalysts.rationale: The first FOMC since forward guidance was removed to publish a full SEP, and therefore the clearest available signal of the Warsh Fed's reaction function. Three voters dissented for a 25bp increase in July and futures drift toward roughly 4.00% by year-end. A hike or a hawkish dot distribution compresses the AU-US policy differential toward +47.5bp and inverts the +18bp 10Y spread, pushing the dollar onto the US-exceptionalism leg of the smile where AUD/USD reliably underperforms. This is the identified cross-horizon inflection point.

catalysts.event: Expiry of US fiscal-year 2026 federal appropriations
catalysts.rationale: Federal funding lapses at fiscal year end, and 2026 has already produced a partial DHS shutdown running from 14 February to 30 April, so the base rate for disruption is empirically high. A shutdown into an already-elevated 30-year yield and a fiscal baseline that has lost $1.7tn of projected tariff revenue by judicial order is the specific configuration in which the term-premium channel dominates and the dollar falls despite widening carry — the single most plausible route to the pair's upside scenario.

catalysts.event: ABS Consumer Price Index, September quarter 2026
catalysts.rationale: The highest-impact Australian data release because of the quarterly cadence — three months of expectations compressed into one print. The September quarter captures the full pass-through of the July energy escalation into transport and input costs, working against base effects from the expiring electricity rebate distortion. A trimmed mean above 3.6% would reopen the RBA hiking case and reverse the compression thesis; a print at or below 3.3% would confirm it.

All 435 House seats and one third of the Senate are contested, determining fiscal and trade policy settings for the remainder of the presidential term. Because judicial rulings have already voided the IEEPA tariff architecture and left roughly $166bn of refunds in dispute, congressional control has unusually direct implications for the revenue path underpinning the term premium currently sitting in the 30-year at 5.27%. Australia has no comparable domestic political risk inside the window, making this a one-sided pair positive.

catalysts.event: Simultaneous expiry of three US-China suspensions (Section 301 exclusions, BIS Affiliates Rule, Section 301 shipbuilding remedy)
catalysts.rationale: A dated, binary trade-policy event. AUD is the most liquid China proxy in the G10, with China taking roughly 30% of Australian goods and services exports at A$196bn, so a failure to extend transmits to AUD faster and harder than to any other G10 currency, while USD absorbs the resulting flight to quality. This is the single catalyst where both legs move the pair the same way, compounding a Chinese economy already growing at 4.3% with a manufacturing PMI back in contraction at 49.2.

catalysts.event: RBA final 2026 decision, then FOMC with the year's final SEP (9 December)
catalysts.rationale: The resolution point for the whole strategic thesis, with the two central banks meeting within twenty-four hours of each other. If the RBA has held at 4.35% since May while the Fed has reached 3.75-4.00%, the differential will have compressed on every axis and the December SEP is where the market reprices the 2027 path. Conversely, if the Fed has not delivered its own 3.8% median by then, the December projections must either mark it down or carry an unfulfilled commitment into 2027 — a credibility event that would be sharply bullish for the pair.

assumptions: Price data is treated as source of truth; three internal inconsistencies in the supplied Twelve Data series (52-week low dating, performance-figure reconciliation, and 200-day SMA level) are disclosed rather than reconciled, and downstream invalidator thresholds are stated against explicit price levels rather than the ambiguous 200-day to insulate them from this uncertainty.

Valuation date versus spot date: dossiers carry a valuation date of 2026-08-01 with spot 0.7035, while the price data runs to 2026-08-05 with a close of 0.70555; all targets, pips and forward outrights in this report are stated relative to 0.70555.

Yield-curve vintage reconciliation: the two dossiers use different US Treasury vintages (29 July FRED vs 31 July Treasury par yield curve); this report uses the Treasury 31 July primary source throughout, making every spread quoted here 6-8bp tighter than the AUD dossier's — the single most consequential interpretive decision in this analysis.

Implied volatility, risk reversals and the AUD/USD three-month cross-currency basis are gaps or single-source proxies: 1M IV (~7.23%) and 3M IV (~8.6%) are carried from single flagged-estimate sources in each dossier; risk-reversal direction is sourced from published commentary rather than a quoted level; the AUD/USD 3M cross-currency basis is a hard, unsourceable gap and Factor 10 confidence is capped at 52/50 accordingly.

Forward points and outrights are CIP-derived from the US Treasury constant-maturity curve against an interpolated Australian short-rate curve, not traded quotes, and will differ from dealer prices by the unobservable cross-currency basis.

The 0.6513-0.6545 fair-value range is a relative BIS REER-deviation netting exercise using different trailing windows in each dossier (30-month AUD vs 5-year USD), not an absolute PPP estimate; the US five-year REER average itself carries an unresolved ~1% discrepancy between cached and re-derived figures.

Positioning data vintages differ (21 July AUD disaggregated vs 28 July USD/AUD legacy) and both precede the 29-31 July dollar decline, so all published dollar length is overstated relative to current conditions; the legacy and disaggregated CFTC series use different taxonomies and are treated as complementary rather than directly comparable.

Bilateral trade figures (IMF DOTS, 2024 vintage) are used as supplied without re-estimation; bilateral investment figures carry mixed vintages (2020-2023) and are used for structural characterisation only, with no flow inference drawn from them.
Scenario probabilities (50/25/25 splits at both horizons) are analyst judgements, not derived from an options-implied distribution, since no full AUD/USD volatility smile was obtainable.

Web-sourced technical levels that conflict with the supplied moving averages (e.g., alternate 100-day/200-day SMA levels) are used only for horizontal support/resistance, chart pattern, momentum and forecast content; all moving-average levels in this report come from the supplied price data per the data-source hierarchy.
